title: Count Substring Rotations in a String

reported.text: Count occurrences in m of all distinct substrings/rotations of n of the same length (e.g., m='aabababbaababab', n='aab').

Start with A = 1 and a sequence of operations (add x, subtract x, multiply by x, divide by x when divisible, negate). Choosing any subsequence of operations in their original order, maximise the final value of A (track both max and min reachable values).

sources.passage:
Nvidia SWE1 DSA Interview Question | 68.5 Lakhs CTC 
You are given an initial integer A = 1.

You will receive B queries, each representing an operation that can be applied to the current value of A. The operations appear in a fixed order, but you are not required to execute every operation. You may choose any subset of the queries, but if you choose an operation, it must be applied in the same order as given.

Your goal is to maximize the final value of A after processing the queries.

The possible operations are:

plus x → Add x to the current value of A

minus x → Subtract x from the current value of A

multiply x → Multiply the current value of A by x

/ x → Divide the current value of A by x

This operation can only be performed if A is divisible by x

N → Negate the current value of A (i.e., A = -A)

You may skip any operation, but the relative order of executed operations must remain the same as in the input.

Return the maximum possible value of A after processing the queries.

He asked me Count and Say from LeetCode.

“Can you do it in linear time?”

I said No, that’s not possible.

He insisted it can.

I walked out depressed — only to later find out he wasn’t from tech.

Round 2

The question was:

Given inequalities like p1 > p2, p2 > p3, p3 < p4 … form an array satisfying all constraints.

I immediately recognized it as a topological sort style problem.
Coded it fast — he was happy.

Then a variant of the Skyline Problem.
I had solved it earlier, so I answered quickly.

Selected for Round 3.

Round 3

He asked:

“Find first max and second max in one pass without using variables.”

I got confused.
He said:

“Use any data structure.”

So I said: set, map, priority queue…

He said:

“Okay, I got what I wanted. You may leave.”

Probably the strangest round of the day.

Results came: Not selected.
All rounds were 20–25 minutes. I genuinely didn’t understand what Round 3 was evaluating.

JPMorgan Chase (Data Analyst Role)
Round 1

“Are you genuinely interested in this role?”

I said I don’t know much about Data Analyst work, but I’m a fast learner.

He then asked OOPs, OS (not sure why), and some probability.
I answered all correctly → moved to Round 2.

There was a total of 3 rounds, There were no % criteria, open for CSE, IT, ECE, EI, EN streams.

* Medium question from the array.
* Knapsack problem with a small twist and we can pick one item more than once.
